analysis: offline futex wait/wake pairing; no capture was run

identity_observations.leader_tid_863769: each of the 598 counted writer waits has a positive same-address wake call temporally within the wait interval; this does not establish which waiter the kernel woke. Leader also issues DQBUF.
identity_observations.writer_tid_863811: all 25,800 writes to fd 12 and futex calls

interpretation: Strong internal synchronization correlation: the output-writer TID has successful waits on two alternating futex addresses, and each wait >=1 ms has a positive same-address FUTEX_WAKE syscall from TID 863769 temporally inside the wait interval. The positive FUTEX_WAKE result does not identify the waiter it woke; a concurrent same-address waiter could have been selected. This does not establish that the wake represents input readiness, decode completion, or the causal source of a read gap. The writer may be idle awaiting upstream work.
limitations: This is offline correlation of one straced run, not causal proof.
strace overhead and per-frame /proc schedstat observer overhead were not independently calibrated.
No stack, syscall instruction pointer, or wchan was captured; syscall callsite and semantic ownership remain unknown.
Frame identity between successful DQBUF calls and raw output remains unproven because the trace omitted DQBUF sequence fields and counted 602 successful dequeues for 600 output frames.
A same-address positive wake observed during the writer wait is not a kernel-confirmed writer wake: FUTEX_WAKE does not report the identity of the awakened waiter, and concurrent waiters may exist.

parser.method: Pair unfinished/resumed futex calls by TID, then associate a writer wait with any positive same-address FUTEX_WAKE from TID 863769 whose syscall entry time falls inside the writer wait interval. This is temporal association only: FUTEX_WAKE return values do not identify which waiter was awakened, and another concurrent same-address waiter may be the waiter selected by the kernel.
